title: Consumer Loyalty Programs and Retail Prices: Evidence from Gasoline Markets
eligible_reason: Not a staggered design. Each regression is a short window around one common program date: the ENI loyalty-program deadline (28 Feb 2017), the Q8 deadline (30 Sep 2018), or the ENI program start (20 Apr 2015). In each window the affiliated brand's stations and the rival distance bands all switch at the same date. Every column also includes four simultaneous treatment indicators (affiliate, rivalIn2, rival2To5, rival5To10), which counts as additional treatments. The deadline indicators equal 1 during the program and 0 after it, so treatment switches off.
design_notes: Table06_Regression.do: xtreg price i.t affiliate rivalIn2 rival2To5 rival5To10, fe cluster(id). Station FE plus daily date FE. The three columns are separate event windows (ENI deadline, Q8 deadline, ENI start). Table 7 adds brand heterogeneity and sample cuts, Table 8 uses gasoline minus diesel price differences, Table 9 interacts every treatment with local competition dummies, and Table 10 interacts them with independent-station status. The ENI and Q8 deadlines are never pooled into one staggered regression. Figures 4-11 are graphical event-window plots.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: One common date per regression. Two brands (ENI 2017, Q8 2018) have deadlines, but they are estimated separately.
data_files: Dataset.csv (4.1 GB; station-day prices, brand, location, competitor counts)
software_notes: Stata for regressions; MATLAB for Tables 1-3 (descriptives).
screener_notes: Screened from package only. A pooled two-deadline design could be built from the data, but the paper does not report one.
